requirements.requirement: On node1, allow only root and opsadmin to schedule cron jobs.
requirements.summary: The final allow-list contains exactly root and opsadmin with root ownership, mode 0600, and the expected SELinux context. Both listed users reach normal crontab handling, while the unlisted antrieb user receives an explicit authorization denial. After restart, the account, allow-list, crond service, and denial behavior persisted.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 were unchanged before and after the work and restart. The implementation used the platform's existing user, file, SELinux, cron, and systemd utilities; no software replacement or upgrade is evidenced.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the node became temporarily unreachable, a different boot identity was observed afterward, and crond plus the access-control configuration recovered. Fixed lifecycle observations independently confirm the boot transition and unchanged platform.
limitations: Package-manager consistency checks timed out both before and after execution, so package health could not be independently compared.

The final post-restart authorization output is partly redacted/malformed, but persistence is still supported by the recovered exact allow-list and service state, while direct unredacted authorization behavior was captured before restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating opsadmin and installing /etc/cron.allow were directly required; the staging file was removed in the same command. The reboot served the mandatory restart-evidence protocol. Other unsuccessful commands were read-only probes and show no mutation. No failed services, added exposure, or abandoned temporary files were observed after execution.
